newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS -NYMEX crude falls to lowest level since Aug.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -NYMEX crude falls to lowest level since Aug.

text.p: Crude futures in New York fell to their lowest level since August on Monday, led by forecasts indicating that the tail end of winter would look more like an early spring.

Monday's losses, which left benchmark Light Crude futures contract on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) down 68 cents at $20.71 a barrel, brought the loss since the start of the year to more than 20 percent.
The mild winter compared with 95/96, which kept heating oil demand moderate, was a principal factor in the decline, together with rising world crude supply.

"Heating oil dragged down the market since, once again, the cold weather we are going to get will only be here for two days and then it gets warm like last week," said Todd Miller, vice president and refined products trader at Morgan Stanley.
Heating oil (March delivery) ended 2.38 cents a gallon lower at 55.47 cents a gallon on NYMEX, its lowest settlement since last July.
April crude's $20.71 settlement was the lowest level for the nearest month since early August.
March gasoline ended off 1.58 cents at 60.24 cents a gallon, the lowest for about six months.

Meanwhile, independent forecaster Weather Services Corp, based in Lexington, Mass., forecast that temperatures would again moderate to above normal this week in the northeastern United States, which has the highest concentration of heating oil demand in the world.

For the week ended February 14, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said heating oil supplies were about even with year ago in the Northeast and 1.3 million barrels above a year ago for all the U.S. regions combined.

Distillate stocks, including heating oil, usually show declines this time of year since refiners have already started to shift production away from heating oil to make gasoline for the summer driving season.
But, traders expect slack demand to temper the stock decline in this week's oil inventory data from the API to be released Tuesday.
Crude has fallen more than $2.00 barrel in the last three sessions. Most traders attribute crude's price deterioration to weak demand for both gasoline and heating oil.
"When distillate (heating oil) finds it's bottom, then crude will," said Morgan Stanley's Miller.
Meanwhile, gasoline is ample in the cash market as supply transitions to spring specifications from winter.

"The only bull of the oil complex was gasoline. Once traders gave up on that, there was nothing left holding up the market" said Prudential Securities analyst Richard Redash, noting gasoline had been benefitting from early anticipation of the traditional spring gasoline rally.
Gasoline rallys in the spring ahead of the summer when demand typically peaks.
Oversupply is also plaguing crude, particulary sour crude.
In fact, IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said on Monday that requests to move oil, gas liquids and refined products on its system in March fell below pipeline capacity.
Low demand and ample refined product supply has limited the need to refine crude. Moreover, heavy winter refinery maintenance has cut refinery operating rates, traders said.
The steep drop in oil prices has, however, made crude a buying opportunity in the short term said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst with Cargill Investor Services.
"We have fallen enough in the last month to justify buying at these levels. We may be at the bottom now, and have a (price) bounce," said Blakeslee.
--((New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620))
